command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp
# Pre-create the declared logs so a run that dies still stages its evidence.
: > createdb.log; : > search.log; : > conv.log

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# PATH export IS needed: aarchbio images have their PATH dropped by the task shell.

echo "== staged bytes must match their pins =="
sha256sum -c pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: a staged file does not match its pin"; exit 1; }
mkdir -p structures && tar -xf structures.tar -C structures
N=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="n_structures"{print $2}' expected.tsv)
GOT=$(ls structures/*.cif | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
printf 'structures_expected\t%s\n' "$N"
printf 'structures_present\t%s\n' "$GOT"
test "$GOT" = "$N" || { echo "FAIL: $GOT structures, expected $N"; exit 1; }

foldseek version 2>&1 | head -2

echo "== build the database from the pinned structures =="
foldseek createdb structures/ db > createdb.log 2>&1
test "$?" = "0" || { tail -20 createdb.log; echo "FAIL: createdb failed"; exit 1; }

echo "== all-against-all with TM-align scoring =="
# --alignment-type 1 is TMalign mode, which reports an actual TM-score. -e inf and a large
# --max-seqs keep every pair, because the check needs to know that nothing OUTSCORES the self
# hit -- a truncated hit list could hide the counterexample.
foldseek search db db aln aln_tmp --alignment-type 1 -e inf --max-seqs 2000 -a > search.log 2>&1
test "$?" = "0" || { tail -25 search.log; echo "FAIL: search failed"; exit 1; }
foldseek convertalis db db aln aln.tsv --format-output "query,target,alntmscore,evalue,bits" > conv.log 2>&1
test "$?" = "0" || { tail -20 conv.log; echo "FAIL: convertalis failed"; exit 1; }
wc -l < aln.tsv | awk '{print "alignment_rows\t"$1}'
head -3 aln.tsv | sed 's/^/  /'

# ------------------------------------------- the algorithmic check: nothing outscores itself
# The queries ARE the database, so every structure must align to itself, and no other target may
# score HIGHER than that self-alignment. This is algorithmic, not empirical -- there is no band.
#
# The claim is deliberately "nothing beats itself", NOT "the best hit is itself": ties are legal
# and this set contains a real one (1pga and 2gb1 are both the protein G B1 domain), so a
# strict best-hit test would fail for a correct tool. The project already paid for that
# distinction once -- an equivalent BLAST check failed 19 of 20 times on arbitrary tie-breaking.
awk -F'\t' '
  { q=$1; t=$2; s=$3+0
    sub(/\.cif(\.gz)?$/,"",q); sub(/\.cif(\.gz)?$/,"",t)
    if (!(q in best) || s > best[q]) { best[q]=s; bestt[q]=t }
    if (q == t) { self[q]=s }
    seen[q]=1
    # foldseek makes one database entry PER CHAIN, so a multi-chain entry yields several
    # queries (4HHB is a tetramer, 1IEP a dimer). Strip any _<chain> suffix to recover the
    # structure it came from, so both counts can be reported.
    pref=q; sub(/_[A-Za-z0-9]+$/,"",pref); struct[pref]=1
  }
  END{
    nq=0; noself=0; beaten=0; imperfect=0
    for (q in seen) {
      nq++
      if (!(q in self)) { printf "FAIL: %s has no self-alignment\n", q; noself++; continue }
      if (self[q] < 0.999) { printf "FAIL: %s self TM-score %.4f, expected 1.0\n", q, self[q]; imperfect++ }
      if (best[q] > self[q] + 1e-9) {
        printf "FAIL: %s is outscored by %s (%.4f > %.4f)\n", q, bestt[q], best[q], self[q]
        beaten++
      }
    }
    ns=0; for (pp in struct) ns++
    printf "queries\t%d\n", nq
    printf "distinct_structures\t%d\n", ns
    printf "missing_self_alignment\t%d\n", noself
    printf "self_tmscore_below_1\t%d\n", imperfect
    printf "queries_outscored_by_another\t%d\n", beaten
    if (noself || imperfect || beaten) exit 1
  }' aln.tsv | tee selfcheck.tsv
test "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: the self-alignment check failed"; exit 1; }
printf 'identity_selfhit\tevery structure aligns to itself at TM-score 1.0 and nothing outscores it\n'

NQ=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="queries"{print $2}' selfcheck.tsv)
NS=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="distinct_structures"{print $2}' selfcheck.tsv)
printf 'chains_per_structure\t%s chains from %s structures\n' "$NQ" "$NS"
# Assert on STRUCTURES, not chains: foldseek indexes one entry per chain, so a multi-chain
# entry legitimately produces several queries and "one query per file" is the wrong
# relationship. Every staged structure must still be represented.
test "$NS" = "$N" || { echo "FAIL: $NS distinct structures in the results, expected $N"; exit 1; }
test "$NQ" -ge "$N" || { echo "FAIL: $NQ queries is fewer than the $N structures staged"; exit 1; }

# The near-tie is worth surfacing rather than hiding: 1pga and 2gb1 are the same domain, so a
# high cross score between them is correct biology and is exactly why the assertion above is an
# inequality rather than an argmax.
printf 'observation\t1pga vs 2gb1 (same protein G B1 domain):\n'
awk -F'\t' '{sub(/\.cif$/,"",$1); sub(/\.cif$/,"",$2);
             if (($1=="1pga" && $2=="2gb1") || ($1=="2gb1" && $2=="1pga"))
               printf "  %s vs %s  TM-score %s\n", $1, $2, $3}' aln.tsv | head -2

{ printf 'observable\tvalue\n'
  printf 'structures\t%s\n' "$GOT"
  printf 'chains\t%s\n' "$NQ"
  printf 'alignment_rows\t%s\n' "$(wc -l < aln.tsv | tr -d ' ')"
  cat selfcheck.tsv
} > score.tsv
cp score.tsv foldseek-diag.txt
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "FOLDSEEK OK"
